data.content_ref: inline:The isolated artifact 084384ac0b1e abstracts from the neighbourhood's concrete verification procedures (execution matching, counting queries, false-claim injection) by extracting their common logical form: every genuine verification is a function f(claim, world_state) -> {accept, reject} where the accept-or-reject output is not a function of the claim alone. The abstraction is grounded in SRC_002's information-theoretic criterion (the check output's information content must exceed the claim's) and SRC_003's discrimination requirement (the verifier must produce negatives, not just agreement), but generalizes beyond execution and counting to any domain where a world-state oracle exists. It is refuted if there exists a domain in which verification is genuine (accepted by the case-level criteria of SRC_001 or SRC_002) but no world-state oracle can be defined — making f(claim, world_state) unconstructible — or if the information-theoretic abstraction of SRC_002 is shown to be neither necessary nor sufficient, undercutting the abstraction's foundation.
